stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They recruited 60 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers then recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They recruited 90 high school students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers then recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later.

Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They recruited 110 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers then recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.
Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.

Researchers investigated whether mindfulness meditation lowers stress. They recruited 84 office workers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition practiced mindfulness meditation for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition listened to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that listened to an audiobook

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

columns.label: Mean score on the final test (%)

rows.group: The group that took practice quizzes
The group that reread the passage

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.
Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

Researchers collected data from 300 families. For each one, they recorded the warmth of parenting, as rated by observers and the child's self-esteem score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.48.
Researchers collected data from 250 adults. For each one, they recorded resting heart rate and self-rated anxiety. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.38.

Researchers investigated whether nausea after a new taste produces an aversion to that taste. They recruited 40 laboratory rats and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Rats in one condition drank sweetened water and were then given an injection that causes mild nausea. Rats in the other condition drank sweetened water and were then given a harmless salt-water injection. The researchers then recorded the volume in milliliters of sweetened water that each rat drank the next day.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They hypothesized that help from an adult would affect problem-solving skill.

**Participants.** The sample was 64 five-year-old children, recruited from one city. Parents gave informed consent, each child gave assent, and the plan was approved by an institutional review board. Families could withdraw at any time.

**Method.** The children were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

**Results.** The group that received hints: mean new puzzles solved (out of 10) = 7.2. The group that practiced alone: mean new puzzles solved (out of 10) = 4.6. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Why do people sometimes fail to help in an emergency?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 80 students were randomly assigned to be alone or with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants who were alone reported the smoke after a mean of 58 seconds; those in groups took a mean of 196 seconds (p = 0.01), and many never reported it.

**Source B.** In interviews after a staged emergency, participants who had not helped often said that they 'assumed someone else had already called for help' or that 'nobody else looked worried, so it could not be serious.'

**Source C.** Researchers observed 300 staged incidents in which a person dropped a bag of shopping in the street. Help was offered in 82 percent of incidents on quiet streets and in 41 percent of incidents on crowded streets.

questions.stem: Ben is tormented by constant worry and feels miserable most of the day. Which criterion for a psychological disorder does this meet?

options.why: Stigma is the negative attitudes and discrimination directed at people who have a psychological disorder.
The DSM is the American Psychiatric Association's manual for classifying and diagnosing psychological disorders.
Correct. Distress is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person.
The ICD is the World Health Organization's international system for classifying all diseases, including mental disorders.

questions.explanation: Distress is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes habituation?

options.text: The replacing of an unwanted response to a stimulus with a new response, by pairing the stimulus with something pleasant
options.why: That describes counterconditioning.

options.text: A learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness
options.why: That describes a taste aversion.

options.text: The decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over
options.why: Correct. This is what habituation means.

options.text: The inborn readiness to learn some associations, such as taste and nausea, more easily than others
options.why: That describes biological preparedness.

questions.explanation: Habituation is the decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes self-concept?

options.text: A questionnaire with many true-false or agree-disagree items that measures a range of traits
options.why: That describes a personality inventory.

options.text: The statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits
options.why: That describes factor analysis.

options.text: The belief in one's own ability to succeed at a particular task
options.why: That describes self-efficacy.

options.text: All the thoughts and feelings a person has in answer to the question 'Who am I?'
options.why: Correct. This is what self-concept means.

questions.explanation: Self-concept is all the thoughts and feelings a person has in answer to the question 'Who am I?'.

questions.stem: Leo finds broccoli unbearably bitter and has an unusually large number of taste buds. He is best described as which of the following?

options.why: Correct. A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.
Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.
Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.
A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.

questions.explanation: A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes animism?

options.text: The belief of young children that lifeless objects have feelings and intentions
options.why: Correct. This is what animism means.

options.text: The understanding that other people have their own thoughts, beliefs and feelings
options.why: That describes theory of mind.

options.text: The understanding that an action can be undone to return things to their original state
options.why: That describes reversibility.

options.text: The understanding that quantity stays the same when shape or arrangement changes
options.why: That describes conservation.

questions.explanation: Animism is the belief of young children that lifeless objects have feelings and intentions.

questions.stem: Without evidence, Hugo is convinced that his coworkers, neighbors and friends are all plotting against him, and he has felt this way for years. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Antisocial personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others.
Dependent personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an excessive need to be taken care of and by clinging, submissive behavior.
Narcissistic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an exaggerated sense of self-importance and a need for admiration.
Correct. Paranoid personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others.

questions.explanation: Paranoid personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes working memory?

options.text: The brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second
options.why: That describes iconic memory.

options.text: The active processing of information held in mind, combining new input with knowledge from long-term memory
options.why: Correct. This is what working memory means.

options.text: The relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences
options.why: That describes long-term memory.

options.text: The sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds
options.why: That describes echoic memory.

questions.explanation: Working memory is the active processing of information held in mind, combining new input with knowledge from long-term memory.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations?

options.why: Taijin kyofusho is the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly in Japan, marked by fear of offending or embarrassing others.
Agoraphobia is the disorder in which a person fears and avoids public places from which escape might be difficult.
Correct. Social anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations.
Generalized anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person feels tense and worried most of the time about many things, for at least six months.

questions.explanation: Social anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations.

questions.stem: After the election result is announced, Tom says, 'I knew all along that she would win,' although he had predicted the opposite. Which bias is this?

options.why: Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.
Correct. Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.
Social desirability bias is the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good.
Self-report bias is the inaccuracy that arises when people describe their own behavior or feelings.

questions.explanation: Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.

questions.stem: Each of twenty witnesses to an accident assumes that someone else has already called for help, so nobody calls. Which concept explains their thinking?

options.why: Groupthink is the kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives.
Social loafing is the tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone.
Correct. Diffusion of responsibility is the reduced sense of personal duty to act when other people are present.
Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.

questions.explanation: Diffusion of responsibility is the reduced sense of personal duty to act when other people are present.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses?

options.why: Correct. A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.
Continuous reinforcement is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced every time it occurs.
A variable-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after an unpredictable number of responses.
A fixed-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced.

questions.explanation: A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.

questions.stem: A clinician explains a patient's depression by her family history, her negative thinking style and her recent job loss together. Which model is this?

options.why: An eclectic approach is the use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem.
Correct. The biopsychosocial model is the view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors.
Comorbidity is the presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time.
The diathesis-stress model is the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience.

questions.explanation: The biopsychosocial model is the view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones?

options.why: The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.
Correct. The serial position effect is the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones.
The spacing effect is the finding that study spread over time produces better long-term memory than study crammed together.
The recency effect is the tendency to remember the last items in a list well.

questions.explanation: The serial position effect is the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones.

questions.stem: A researcher destroys a tiny part of a rat's hypothalamus and observes how its eating changes. Which research technique is this?

options.why: Correct. Lesioning is the destruction of a small area of brain tissue to study its function.
Neuroplasticity is the brain's ability to change by reorganizing after damage or building new pathways through experience.
A case study is an in-depth study of one individual, such as a patient with unusual brain damage.
An EEG is a recording of the electrical waves that sweep across the brain's surface.

questions.explanation: Lesioning is the destruction of a small area of brain tissue to study its function.

questions.stem: Four studies of child development report these correlation coefficients: −0.78, +0.12, +0.05, −0.93. Which coefficient shows the strongest relationship?

options.why: −0.78 is closer to zero.
+0.12 is closer to zero.
Correct. Strength is the distance from zero, whatever the sign; −0.93 is farthest from zero.
+0.05 is closer to zero.

questions.explanation: The sign of a correlation shows its direction; its distance from zero shows its strength. −0.93 is farthest from zero.

questions.stem: In a photo, two identical cars appear, and the one that looks smaller is judged to be farther away. Which depth cue is this?

options.why: Correct. Relative size is the monocular depth cue in which the object that casts the smaller image is seen as farther away.
Convergence is the binocular depth cue based on how far the eyes turn inward to focus on a near object.
Retinal disparity is the binocular depth cue based on the difference between the images in the two eyes.
Interposition is the monocular depth cue in which an object that partly blocks another is seen as closer.

questions.explanation: Relative size is the monocular depth cue in which the object that casts the smaller image is seen as farther away.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard?

options.why: A superordinate goal is a shared goal that can be reached only if groups cooperate, which reduces conflict between them.
Correct. Conformity is the adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard.
Individualism is the cultural pattern that gives priority to personal goals and defines identity by personal traits.
A social trap is a situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone.

questions.explanation: Conformity is the adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard.

questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the assistants who recorded the results knew which condition each participant was in. What is this procedure called?

options.why: In a single-blind procedure only the participants are unaware.
Correct. Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.
Random sampling is how participants are chosen from a population.
That is a therapy technique, not a research control.

questions.explanation: Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the disorder in which a person cannot remember important personal information, usually after trauma and with no physical cause, sometimes with travel away from home (fugue)?

options.why: A compulsion is a repeated action that a person feels driven to perform to reduce anxiety.
Obsessive-compulsive disorder is the disorder in which a person has unwanted repeated thoughts and feels driven to perform repeated actions.

Correct. Dissociative amnesia is the disorder in which a person cannot remember important personal information, usually after trauma and with no physical cause, sometimes with travel away from home (fugue).
Posttraumatic stress disorder is the disorder in which a person has flashbacks, nightmares, watchfulness and avoidance for more than a month after a terrifying event.

questions.explanation: Dissociative amnesia is the disorder in which a person cannot remember important personal information, usually after trauma and with no physical cause, sometimes with travel away from home (fugue).

questions.stem: The group that stayed awake responded more slowly. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The amount of sleep caused the difference in reaction time
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The amount of sleep and reaction time are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables?

options.why: The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.
The directionality problem is the difficulty in a correlational study of knowing which variable influences the other.
Correct. A scatterplot is a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables.
A negative correlation is a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls.

questions.explanation: A scatterplot is a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 110 adult volunteers. What does this most limit?

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: A therapist asks her client to relax and say every thought that enters his head, however trivial or embarrassing. Which technique is this?

options.why: Correct. Free association is the psychodynamic technique in which the client says whatever comes to mind.
Active listening is the technique of echoing, restating and seeking clarification of what the client says.
Dream interpretation is the psychodynamic technique of analyzing dreams to uncover unconscious wishes and conflicts.
Hypnosis is a state of heightened suggestibility that can help reduce pain and anxiety but does not reliably recover memories.

questions.explanation: Free association is the psychodynamic technique in which the client says whatever comes to mind.

questions.stem: Marc reads the assigned novel only because he wants a good grade. Which kind of motivation is this?

options.why: Correct. Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.
An approach-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features.
An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.
Intrinsic motivation is the desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying.

questions.explanation: Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.

options.text: The group asked the question with the word 'smashed'
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: The group asked the question with the word 'contacted'
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: After failing a quiz, Ty says, 'I am just not a math person,' and stops trying. Which belief does this show?

options.why: Correct. A fixed mindset is the belief that intelligence is set and cannot be changed.
Stereotype threat is the worry about confirming a negative stereotype about one's group, which can lower performance.
An aptitude test is a test that predicts a person's ability to learn or perform in the future.
A growth mindset is the belief that intelligence can be developed through effort and learning.

questions.explanation: A fixed mindset is the belief that intelligence is set and cannot be changed.

questions.stem: Receptors in Tia's fingertip detect a pinprick, and a signal travels toward her spinal cord. Which cells carry this incoming signal?

options.why: Correct. Sensory neurons is the neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord.
Glial cells is the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons.
Motor neurons is the neurons that carry outgoing information from the brain and spinal cord to the muscles and glands.
Interneurons is the neurons inside the brain and spinal cord that pass messages between sensory inputs and motor outputs.

questions.explanation: Sensory neurons is the neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord.

questions.stem: After the study behind his favorite diet is shown to be fraudulent, Raj still insists that the diet works. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Cognitive dissonance is the discomfort a person feels when their actions and attitudes conflict, which motivates a change in one of them.
Out-group homogeneity bias is the tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike.
In-group bias is the tendency to favor the members of one's own group.
Correct. Belief perseverance is the tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited.

questions.explanation: Belief perseverance is the tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the central nervous system?

options.text: The sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body
options.why: That describes the peripheral nervous system.

options.text: The division of the autonomic nervous system that calms the body and conserves energy
options.why: That describes the parasympathetic nervous system.
Correct. This is what the central nervous system means.

options.text: The division of the peripheral nervous system that controls glands and internal organs without conscious effort
options.why: That describes the autonomic nervous system.

questions.explanation: The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord.

questions.stem: Which stage of sleep is called paradoxical sleep because the brain is active while the body is nearly paralyzed?

options.why: NREM stage 3 is the deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake.
The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep.
Correct. REM sleep is the sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles.
REM rebound is the tendency to have more REM sleep after being deprived of it.

questions.explanation: REM sleep is the sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles.

questions.stem: On a very easy test, most students score near 100 but a few score very low, so the mean is below the median. Which shape does the distribution have?

options.why: Correct. A negative skew is a distribution with a few extremely low scores, which pull the mean below the median.
The standard deviation is the measure of how much scores vary around the mean.
The normal curve is the symmetrical, bell-shaped distribution in which most scores fall near the mean.
The range is the difference between the highest and lowest scores.

questions.explanation: A negative skew is a distribution with a few extremely low scores, which pull the mean below the median.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion?

options.why: Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.
Universal emotions is the basic emotions, such as happiness, sadness, fear and anger, whose facial expressions are recognized across cultures.
A display rule is a cultural rule about which emotions may be shown, when and to whom.
Correct. An elicitor is an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion.

questions.explanation: An elicitor is an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes adrenaline?

options.text: The hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger
options.why: That describes ghrelin.

options.text: The hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress
options.why: Correct. This is what adrenaline means.

options.text: The hormone that promotes bonding, trust and social attachment
options.why: That describes oxytocin.

options.text: The hormone released by fat cells that signals fullness and reduces hunger
options.why: That describes leptin.

questions.explanation: Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion?

options.why: Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.
Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.
Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.
Correct. Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.

questions.explanation: Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes generativity versus stagnation?

options.text: Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are
options.why: That describes identity versus role confusion.

options.text: Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret
options.why: That describes integrity versus despair.

options.text: Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work
options.why: Correct. This is what generativity versus stagnation means.

options.text: Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships
options.why: That describes intimacy versus isolation.

questions.explanation: Generativity versus stagnation is Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the neurotransmitter that helps control alertness and arousal?

options.why: Correct. Norepinephrine is the neurotransmitter that helps control alertness and arousal.
Glutamate is the brain's main excitatory neurotransmitter, which is involved in memory.
Serotonin is the neurotransmitter that affects mood, hunger and sleep.
Substance P is the neurotransmitter that carries pain messages to the brain.

questions.explanation: Norepinephrine is the neurotransmitter that helps control alertness and arousal.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.why: Experiments also use numerical data.
Experiments also test hypotheses.
Sample size does not determine the research method.

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: Raccoons trained to drop coins into a box began rubbing the coins together as if washing food, despite getting no reward for it. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Superstitious behavior is a behavior that is repeated because it happened by chance just before a reward.
Shaping is the reinforcing of closer and closer approximations of a desired behavior.
Correct. Instinctive drift is the tendency of a trained animal to return to its natural, inborn behaviors.
A secondary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as money or praise, that gets its power through association with other rewards.

questions.explanation: Instinctive drift is the tendency of a trained animal to return to its natural, inborn behaviors.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the stable negative charge inside a neuron when it is not firing?

options.why: Correct. The resting potential is the stable negative charge inside a neuron when it is not firing.
The all-or-nothing principle is the rule that a neuron either fires at full strength or does not fire at all.
Depolarization is the change in which positive ions rush into the axon and make the inside less negative.
The refractory period is the brief pause after a neuron fires during which it cannot fire again.

questions.explanation: The resting potential is the stable negative charge inside a neuron when it is not firing.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a meta-analysis?

options.text: The bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client
options.why: That describes the therapeutic alliance.

options.text: A therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view
options.why: That describes cultural humility.

options.text: The movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care
options.why: That describes deinstitutionalization.

options.text: A statistical procedure that combines the results of many studies to reach an overall conclusion
options.why: Correct. This is what a meta-analysis means.

questions.explanation: A meta-analysis is a statistical procedure that combines the results of many studies to reach an overall conclusion.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards?

options.why: Aversion therapy is the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus.
Biofeedback is the technique of using electronic monitoring to show a person their body's signals so that they can learn to control them.
Correct. A token economy is the behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards.
Applied behavior analysis is the use of the principles of conditioning to increase helpful behaviors and reduce harmful ones.

questions.explanation: A token economy is the behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards.

questions.stem: Identical twins raised apart develop different accents, diets and hobbies that match their adoptive families. This finding most supports the influence of which of the following?

options.why: The evolutionary perspective is the approach that explains behavior through natural selection of traits that helped ancestors survive and reproduce.
A twin study is research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity.
Correct. Nurture is the influence of environmental factors, such as upbringing and experience, on behavior and mental processes.
Nature is the influence of inherited genetic factors on behavior and mental processes.

questions.explanation: Nurture is the influence of environmental factors, such as upbringing and experience, on behavior and mental processes.

questions.stem: Newly hatched ducklings follow the first moving thing they see, a researcher, as if he were their mother. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The rooting reflex is a newborn's automatic turning of the head toward a touch on the cheek, to find food.
Correct. Imprinting is the process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see.
A teratogen is a harmful agent, such as alcohol or a virus, that can damage an embryo or fetus.
The visual cliff is the laboratory apparatus with a glass-covered drop that is used to test depth perception in infants.

questions.explanation: Imprinting is the process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes dichromatism?

options.text: The theory that color is processed in opposing pairs: red–green, blue–yellow and black–white
options.why: That describes the opponent-process theory.

options.text: The inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage
options.why: That describes prosopagnosia.

options.text: A rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray
options.why: That describes monochromatism.

options.text: A form of color vision deficiency in which one of the three types of cones does not work
options.why: Correct. This is what dichromatism means.

questions.explanation: Dichromatism is a form of color vision deficiency in which one of the three types of cones does not work.

questions.stem: A charity first asks people to sign a petition and a week later asks the same people for a donation. Which technique is this?

options.why: Correct. The foot-in-the-door technique is the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted.
The peripheral route to persuasion is persuasion that works through surface cues, such as an attractive or famous speaker.
Normative social influence is the influence that comes from a person's desire to gain approval or avoid rejection.
The door-in-the-face technique is the strategy of making a large request that will be refused so that a smaller request is more likely to be accepted.

questions.explanation: The foot-in-the-door technique is the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as study that is spread out over several sessions?

options.why: Chunking is the organizing of items into familiar, manageable units.
Massed practice is study that is crammed into one long session.
Correct. Distributed practice is study that is spread out over several sessions.
The method of loci is the mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route.

questions.explanation: Distributed practice is study that is spread out over several sessions.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the consolidation theory?

options.text: The theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories
options.why: Correct. This is what the consolidation theory means.

options.text: The strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep
options.why: That describes memory consolidation.

options.text: The repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep
options.why: That describes restoration.

options.text: The theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep
options.why: That describes the activation-synthesis theory.

questions.explanation: The consolidation theory is the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

questions.stem: Before her wedding, Rosa feels nervous and excited, and the feeling gives her energy to prepare. Which kind of stress is this?

options.why: Distress is the negative stress that harms well-being and performance.
A stressor is an event or situation that a person sees as threatening or challenging.
Health psychology is the field that studies how behavior, thoughts and emotions affect physical health and illness.
Correct. Eustress is the positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge.

questions.explanation: Eustress is the positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge.

questions.stem: Rex looks for excitement through wild parties and reckless, uninhibited behavior. Which form of sensation seeking is this?

options.why: Correct. Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.
Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.
Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.
Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.

questions.explanation: Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses?

options.why: Correct. Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.
Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.
Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.
Repression is the defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness.

questions.explanation: Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.80. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the medulla?

options.text: The base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing
options.why: Correct. This is what the medulla means.

options.text: The master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus
options.why: That describes the pituitary gland.

options.text: The brain's sensory relay station, which directs incoming signals to the cortex
options.why: That describes the thalamus.

options.text: The network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness
options.why: That describes the reticular activating system.

questions.explanation: The medulla is the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.why: Experiments also test hypotheses.
Sample size does not determine the research method.
Experiments also use numerical data.

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.
This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.
A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an institutional review board?

options.text: The requirement that researchers keep the physical and psychological risks to participants as low as possible
options.why: That describes protection from harm.

options.text: The explaining of a study's purpose, and any deception, to participants after it ends
options.why: That describes debriefing.

options.text: A person who seems to be a participant but is secretly working for the researcher
options.why: That describes a confederate.

options.text: The committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically
options.why: Correct. This is what an institutional review board means.

questions.explanation: An institutional review board is the committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.text: The behavior of an adult model
options.why: Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.
This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.
This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.

options.text: The number of participants in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the general adaptation syndrome?

options.text: The third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely
options.why: That describes the exhaustion phase.

options.text: Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion
options.why: Correct. This is what the general adaptation syndrome means.

options.text: The first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated
options.why: That describes the alarm reaction.

options.text: The second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor
options.why: That describes the resistance phase.

questions.explanation: The general adaptation syndrome is Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.

questions.stem: According to Freud, a person may be unable to recall a painful childhood event because the mind has blocked it from consciousness. What did Freud call this?

options.why: Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.
Correct. Repression is in psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness.
The tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon is the temporary inability to retrieve a word that one is sure one knows.
Retroactive interference is the disruption of older memories by new learning.

questions.explanation: Repression is in psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes fidelity?

options.text: The ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate
options.why: That describes integrity.

options.text: The ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises
options.why: Correct. This is what fidelity means.

options.text: The ethical principle that psychologists must protect privacy, confidentiality and the right of people to make their own choices
options.why: That describes respect for people's rights and dignity.

options.text: The ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm
options.why: That describes nonmaleficence.

questions.explanation: Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them?

options.why: Pretend play is the play in which children act out imaginary roles and situations.
Emerging adulthood is the period from about 18 to the mid-twenties, between adolescence and full independence.
Correct. The imaginary audience is the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them.
Adverse childhood experiences is the stressful or traumatic events in childhood, such as abuse or neglect, that raise the risk of later problems.

questions.explanation: The imaginary audience is the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.
A case study examines one individual in depth.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.
This is the independent variable.
This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

options.text: The number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes contact comfort?

options.text: The insecure attachment style in which a child is very upset by separation and is not easily comforted on reunion
options.why: That describes anxious attachment.

options.text: The distress that infants show when a familiar caregiver leaves, which peaks around 13 months
options.why: That describes separation anxiety.

options.text: The insecure attachment style in which a child shows confused, contradictory behavior toward the caregiver
options.why: That describes disorganized attachment.

options.text: The comfort from physical touch that Harlow showed is more important to attachment than feeding
options.why: Correct. This is what contact comfort means.

questions.explanation: Contact comfort is the comfort from physical touch that Harlow showed is more important to attachment than feeding.

questions.stem: A child gets out of bed during deep sleep, walks to the kitchen, and remembers nothing in the morning. Which sleep disorder is this?

options.why: Insomnia is a sleep disorder with ongoing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.
Correct. Somnambulism is sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep.
Sleep apnea is a sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings.
REM sleep behavior disorder is a sleep disorder in which the normal paralysis of REM sleep is missing, so the person acts out dreams.

questions.explanation: Somnambulism is sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test?

options.why: Construct validity is the extent to which a test measures the concept it claims to measure.
Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.
Standardization is the giving and scoring of a test in the same way for everyone, and the comparison of scores with a pretested group.
Correct. Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.

questions.explanation: Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes cognitive restructuring?

options.text: The therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder
options.why: That describes dialectical behavior therapy.

options.text: The technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones
options.why: Correct. This is what cognitive restructuring means.

options.text: The therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior
options.why: That describes cognitive-behavioral therapy.

options.text: The pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression
options.why: That describes the cognitive triad.

questions.explanation: Cognitive restructuring is the technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones.

questions.stem: After being corrected, a toddler stops calling every four-legged animal a dog and learns a separate category for cows. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A schema is a mental framework that organizes and interprets information.
Correct. Accommodation is the changing of an existing schema to fit new information.
A prototype is the best or most typical example of a category.
Assimilation is the interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema.

questions.explanation: Accommodation is the changing of an existing schema to fit new information.

options.why: A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.
No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.
A case study examines one individual in depth.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: Sam is warm, quick to forgive and always willing to help. He would score high on which Big Five trait?

options.why: Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.
Conscientiousness is the Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined.
Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.
Correct. Agreeableness is the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative.

questions.explanation: Agreeableness is the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative.

questions.stem: Which ethical requirement applies to this study?

options.text: No ethical rules apply to research with animals
options.why: Animal research is governed by ethical guidelines.

options.text: The animals must be debriefed after the study
options.why: Debriefing applies to human participants.

options.text: The animals must be treated humanely, and the plan must be approved by a committee that reviews animal research
options.why: Correct. Research with animals requires humane care and approval by a review committee.

options.text: Each animal must give informed consent
options.why: Animals cannot give consent.

questions.explanation: Research with animals requires humane care and approval by a review committee.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of problem-solving skill

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of problem-solving skill.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Problem-solving skill was defined as the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The group that received hints solved more new puzzles. On average, the value was 7.2 for the group that received hints and 4.6 for the group that practiced alone, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent and assent: parents consented and each child agreed to take part. (Also acceptable: approval by an institutional review board; the right to withdraw.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 64 five-year-old children from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The group that received hints solved more new puzzles. (7.2 compared with 4.6).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that help from an adult affects problem-solving skill. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to help from an adult. The finding illustrates scaffolding within the zone of proximal development: temporary support lets a child master what they could not yet do alone.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Why do people sometimes fail to help in an emergency?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: People are less likely to help when others are present, because each person feels less responsible and looks to others to decide how to act.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, participants who were alone reported smoke after 58 seconds, but those in groups of five took 196 seconds.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility: when others are present, each person feels less personal responsibility to act.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, participants said that 'nobody else looked worried, so it could not be serious.'

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through informational social influence: in an unclear situation, people use the behavior of others as evidence of what is happening, so if nobody reacts, each person concludes there is no emergency.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
